tasks.short: Develop radiation treatment plans with the oncology team

steps.what: Retrieve patient planning information and current treatment requirements
Consult oncology team about treatment objectives and constraints
Develop and write the patient-specific radiation treatment plan
Evaluate treatment plan consistency and unresolved planning tradeoffs
Write planning rationale and team consultation record
Hand off exact treatment plan version for team review

tasks.design: Configure native case views and reusable non-clinical plan structures in {OTHER}, the existing treatment-planning system, plus rationale headings in {DOCS}. The dosimetrist develops the patient-specific plan and evaluates it; consultation, actual plan writing, rationale recording and final review handoff are separate steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case references and repeated plan-document structures require manual handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning-system views and compatible templates may reduce a small amount of assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Patient-specific treatment tradeoffs and technical consistency with the team's requirements.
tasks.human_edge: Accountable planning judgement and collaboration with the oncology team.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated plan assembly while retaining clinical and technical judgement.

reach.learn: Keep plan version and unresolved issues explicit

evidence.claim: Native treatment-planning views and non-clinical document templates may reduce repeated assembly; the digest supplies no dosimetry planning time case.
The digest identifies medical-device requirements as relevant to medical-purpose software; the proposal stays within supported existing functions pending local assessment.

assumptions: Includes the actual plan and consultation record. The handoff is for team review, not authority to release treatment or an extra self-approval of an ordinary save.

The dosimetrist captures patient identifier, source-study version, prescription version and current planning requirements in s1, clarified constraints in s2, the actual plan version in s3 and rationale in s5. Capture and validation time remain counted. Missing or incompatible data are resolved manually before planning continues.
Native views and supported non-clinical structures come first; no new dose algorithm, automatic optimisation, generative plan or unlisted machine action is proposed.
Existing calculations remain part of today's planning software, with no new saving claimed for their runtime. Same-system author saves are fully retained within s3 and s5.
unknowns: Local review and clinical release workflow
research_questions: Do supported native structures reduce repeated entry while preserving exact source and plan versions?

incremental.description: Maintain supported layouts and test version changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact draft plan version, source versions, rationale and unresolved questions delivered for team review; any change requires a new handoff check and does not authorise treatment

High retains13/15 retrieval,38/40 plan writing and4/5 rationale when native structures fit: gross5 less2=3. Consultation, plan evaluation and review handoff remain full. Already-configured functions offer no new benefit.

steps.what: Retrieve simulation request, imaging references and case requirements
Supervise or perform imaging simulation for tumor localizations
Assess imaging suitability and localisation uncertainties
Write simulation record and image-reference details
Communicate simulation findings and current image references

tasks.design: Configure a native case view and simulation-record structure in {OTHER}, the existing imaging and treatment-planning systems. Physical simulation, image suitability judgement, record writing and the final team handoff remain separately priced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case references and repeated simulation record headings require clerical handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported native views and fields may reduce small amounts of lookup and entry.
tasks.still_hard: Patient-specific imaging, physical setup and interpretation of uncertain localisation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an unsuitable simulation and communicating its limitations.
tasks.altitude: Simplify the supporting record while retaining simulation expertise.

reach.learn: Keep source-study references and limitations traceable

evidence.claim: The digest names scanner-protocol distribution capability in Siemens teamplay Protocols; this is adjacent support, not evidence of automated radiotherapy simulation.
Simulation lookup and record-field savings are unmeasured E1 scenarios.

assumptions: The episode includes the actual simulation record and team handoff, rather than folding documentation into the physical simulation.

The dosimetrist captures patient, request and study identifiers in s1, produces observed simulation conditions in s2 and checked findings in s3, then records date, study version, relevant conditions and limitations in s4. Capture is included; missing or mismatched references require manual resolution.
Native case and record configuration comes first; existing acquisition and reconstruction runtime is already today's software and has no new saving.
No new imaging interpretation, protocol-selection model or unlisted automatic alert is introduced. Same-system saves are retained within s4 without self-approval.
unknowns: Current native record fields and case linking
Actual responsibility for simulation and handoff
research_questions: Can native views reduce reference lookup without obscuring a wrong or outdated image study?

incremental.description: Maintain supported case and record fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact simulation record, image-study references and stated limitations shared with the team; changes require a new final-version check

tasks.short: Record patient information and administered radiation doses

steps.what: Retrieve administered-dose information and patient record references
Reconcile patient identity, dose event and source discrepancies
outputs: reconciled recording details or unresolved discrepancy

steps.what: Record patient information and confirmed radiation dose details
inputs: reconciled recording details or unresolved discrepancy

steps.what: Check patient entry against the confirmed source event
Save the checked entry in the same patient record

tasks.design: Configure native source views and a concise entry layout in {OTHER}, the existing treatment-record and patient-record systems. The dosimetrist reconciles the delivered event and writes the record; the ordinary same-system save stays fully retained and ungated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source references and patient information require repeated navigation and manual entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported native views and entry fields may reduce handling where it remains manual.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving mismatched identity, event versions and discrepancies without assuming a planned dose was delivered.
tasks.human_edge: Responsibility for a faithful patient record.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated record handling with a clearer source trail.

reach.task: Trace a clinical record to its source
reach.learn: Preserve event identity and correction history

evidence.claim: The digest describes patient-dossier obligations; it does not demonstrate a radiation-dose recording integration or its time saving.
Native source navigation and structured manual entry may reduce record handling where not already configured.

assumptions: Baseline is the actual patient-information record task, including lookup, reconciliation, writing, checking and a small same-system save.

The treatment team produces the delivered-event record during delivery, with its capture time owned by that delivery task; the dosimetrist retrieves and verifies patient identifier, treatment-event identifier, plan version, date, administered dose, units and source version in s1-s2, whose time is counted here. Missing or conflicting delivered-event evidence is resolved manually; planned values are never substituted.
Native linked views and concise entry fields come first. No implicit machine field fill, dose calculation, automatic discrepancy flag or external send is proposed.
Existing automatic interfaces offer no new saving. The save's1 percent is fully retained; the author does not approve their own save.
unknowns: How much entry is already automatic
research_questions: Can native views reduce navigation and entry while preserving exact delivered-event identity and dose units?

incremental.description: Maintain native source views and entry fields

High retains18/20 source handling and32/40 entry when native references and fields fit: gross10 less2=8. Reconciliation, final checking and the ordinary save remain full. An already automatic interface has no new eligible benefit.

tasks.short: Advise the oncology team on modifying and immobilisation devices

steps.what: Retrieve treatment plan context and current device references
Evaluate device suitability and patient-specific planning considerations
Advise oncology team members and answer device-use questions
Write device advice, rationale and unresolved questions

tasks.design: Configure current device references and an advice-record structure in {DOCS}, linked to {OTHER}, the treatment-planning system. Suitability judgement and team advice remain human; writing the actual rationale record is separate from the discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Device references and repeated advice-record headings require manual handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native source links and concise record fields may reduce supporting clerical effort.
tasks.still_hard: Device suitability for the particular patient and treatment context.
tasks.human_edge: Technical judgement and clear communication of limitations.
tasks.altitude: More traceable advice with less repeated source and note handling.

reach.learn: Distinguish advice from an authorised plan change

evidence.claim: Native reference links and advice-record headings may reduce clerical support; the digest does not supply a dosimetry device-advice product case.

assumptions: Includes actual device advice and its existing rationale record, not an invented approval or a hidden plan modification.

The dosimetrist captures patient and plan version, device reference version and question in s1; produces chosen advice in s2 and clarified points in s3; records rationale, limitations and unresolved issues in s4. All capture stays counted; missing references require manual clarification.
Native reference and note configuration comes first. No model recommends a device, alters a plan or performs an unlisted send.
The author saves the internal note without a self-gate; its negligible save time remains fully retained in s4.
unknowns: Whether this advice is recorded in the planning system or another document
Actual authority and team handoff practice
research_questions: Do linked references and note headings reduce handling without obscuring plan version or device limitations?

incremental.description: Maintain authorised references and note fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient-specific advice, plan reference and limitations communicated to the team; changes require a renewed check and do not themselves authorise plan modification

High retains14/15 lookup and17/20 recording with current links and usable rationale headings: gross4 less1=3. Device suitability judgement and actual team advice stay fully retained.
